html:
The Brazzaville Conference was a meeting of French colonial officials called by Charles de Gaulle in Brazzaville in early 1944, to plan the future of the French empire in Africa after the war.

Africa had kept Free France alive, and Brazzaville had been its first capital. The conference promised an end to forced labour, the native legal code and some African representation in the French parliament.

It ruled out self-government, even in the future. Yet its reforms led to the French Union of 1946, African deputies in Paris such as Barthélemy Boganda and Léopold Senghor, and a path that ended in independence in 1960.
sum: The Brazzaville Conference was a meeting of French colonial officials called by Charles de Gaulle in Brazzaville in early 1944, to plan the future of the French empire in Africa after the war.
